reviews.text: The Giant Wild Goose Pagoda, or Dayanta, is truly an unmissable experience that provides a sense of history even deeper than the City Wall. This monumental seven-story structure, housed within the Da Ci’en Temple complex, is not just architecture; it is the physical symbol of the Tang Dynasty's golden age and the legendary journey of the monk Xuanzang. Built in 652 AD, the pagoda was designed to safely store the hundreds of Buddhist scriptures (sutras) and relics Xuanzang brought back from his seventeen-year pilgrimage to India, along the ancient Silk Road. It's my buckle list to be able to visit this pagoda, a testament to profound religious devotion and monumental early Chinese engineering, having survived numerous earthquakes over the centuries. The Pagoda sits within the tranquil and beautifully maintained grounds of the Da Ci’en Temple. Do take time to wander the halls, appreciate the stone steles engraved with historical texts (including two featuring writings by Emperor Taizong and Gaozong), and observe the traditional rituals still practiced here. If you can stay till evening, the fountain show at the North Square is massive. It's a musical fountain display, set against the backdrop of the gloriously illuminated pagoda, is absolutely spectacular. It’s a wonderful fusion of classical Chinese music, light, and water (check for seasonal showtimes; they are often held around 8:30 PM/9:00 PM). My getting to the Pagoda is exceptionally easy compared to other sites. Took Xi'an Metro Line 3 or 4 directly to Dayanta Station (Giant Wild Goose Pagoda Station). I Use Exit B, and follow the signs—you'll reach the North Square in just a few minutes.

I visited the Giant Wild Goose Pagoda once, and even a single visit was enough to feel the depth of history held within this landmark. Rising above the Da Ci’en Temple complex, the seven‑story pagoda has a quiet dignity — simple, solid, and unmistakably ancient. Standing in front of it, you sense how many centuries of pilgrims, monks, and travelers have passed through the same courtyard. The temple grounds themselves are beautiful: clean, peaceful, and carefully maintained, with flowers, old trees, and landscaped gardens that soften the edges of the historic structures. Walking through the courtyards feels calm despite the popularity of the site. There’s a gentle rhythm to the place — incense drifting, bells ringing, visitors moving slowly from hall to hall. Climbing the pagoda is a memorable part of the visit. The steps are narrow and steep, but the view from the top is worth it — a wide look over Xi’an and the surrounding temple complex. Even if you choose not to climb, the pagoda’s presence from below is impressive enough. What stayed with me most was the blend of spirituality and everyday life. Around the pagoda, you see people praying, strolling, taking photos, or simply enjoying the gardens. It’s a living space, not just a monument. And knowing that Xuanzang’s Buddhist scriptures were once stored here adds a quiet weight to the experience. Even with just one visit, the Giant Wild Goose Pagoda leaves a lasting impression — a place where history, faith, and the atmosphere of Xi’an come together in a way that feels both grounded and timeless.

Visiting Xi'an is incomplete without exploring the magnificent Giant Wild Goose Pagoda. A testament to ancient Indian civilization, this Royal Buddhism temple from the Tang dynasty showcases the city's rich history. Despite surviving earthquakes, the pagoda's distinct tilt towards the west adds a captivating charm. A notable highlight is the bronze statue of Xuanzang, the protagonist in the timeless novel "Journey to the West," providing a tangible link to literary and historical narratives. Practical amenities, such as real toilets, enhance the visitor experience. As the sun sets, the site transforms into a captivating spectacle with a mesmerizing light and water show. The vibrant surroundings come to life with street vendors, delectable food, talented artists, and lively acrobats. The energetic atmosphere makes the entire area a hub of activity, offering a dynamic experience that complements the historical significance of the Giant Wild Goose Pagoda.

According to wiki, "One of the pagoda's many functions was to hold sutras and figurines of Gautama Buddha that were brought to China from India by the seventh-century Buddhist monk, scholar, traveller, and translator Xuanzang. Today, the interior walls of the pagoda feature engraved statues of Buddha by the renowned 7th-century artist Yan Liben." Although the pagoda itself in its current form is not as old as the Small Wild Goose Pagoda, it every bit as beautiful and historic. The Daci'en Temple (of which the pagoda is part) has a long history as a religious and scholarly center of China. Although many of the smaller buildings are quite new, the pagoda itself can trace its history back over 1300 years, and aside from renovations here and there, as well as repairs made after a large earthquake in the 1500s, it remains largely the same as it has for centuries. The tower is very imposing looking with a noticeable lean, and really stands out above the surrounding area of Xi'an. It is also incredibly beautiful. The entry price to the scenic area is about 40 kuai if I recall, although you have to pay for a separate ticket inside if you want to climb the pagoda itself. There is also an enormous water display to the north of the pagoda which plays an elaborate water show every couple hours if you're into that kind of stuff. Definitely a must-see attraction when in Xi'an

A monolith of time and devotion, the Giant Wild Goose Pagoda rises from Xi’an’s heart, its weathered bricks whispering of a Silk Road long vanished yet still pulsing beneath the city’s skin. Built in 652 AD, it was never just a temple but a vault for ideas—where Xuanzang’s manuscripts, carried from the Indian subcontinent, reshaped Chinese thought, and where each tier ascends toward something beyond the material. Unlike the gleaming towers that now punctuate Xi’an’s skyline, the pagoda remains resolute, a structure that has outlasted dynasties, tremors, and the shifting tides of faith. By day, it is a meditation in geometry, its tapered form casting precise shadows across the plaza. By night, the air vibrates with the cadence of fountain symphonies, modern choreography against an ancient silhouette.

The Big Wild Goose Pagoda is a square pavilion-style tower with a brick imitation wood structure. It consists of three parts: the tower base, the tower body, and the tower brake. The whole tower is 64.7 meters high, with a base height of 4.2 meters, a length of about 48.7 meters from north to south, and a length of about 45.7 meters from east to west. The base of the tower is 25.5 meters long on each side and is in the shape of a square cone. The height of the tower is 4.87 meters. There are 9 rooms on the 1st and 2nd floors, 7 rooms on the 3rd and 4th floors, and five rooms on the 5th, 6th, 7th and 8th floors. Each floor has coupon doors on all sides.The famous Xi'an Big Wild Goose Pagoda is located in the Daci'en Temple in the south of the city, also known as the Daci'en Pagoda.

The Giant Wild Goose Pagoda was founded by Tripitaka, the actual monk whose travels were romanticized in those stories, upon his return from his actual odyssey to reform Chinese Buddhism by bringing scriptures from India back to China in the Tang Dynasty. The original Pagoda is a must-see. Onsite tours provide the rich backstory, with lavishly decorated rooms and murals depicting both Tripitaka's story as well as essential Creation myths and the story of Siddhartha himself. What was inevitable was the commercialism, in the 'Buddhist teaching' that resulted in recommendations to purchase religious relics at various price points, to the basement of the pagoda being converted to essentially a gift shop.

La grande pagode de l'oie sauvage se trouve au sud de la ville, à l'extérieur de la muraille. Une station de métro permet d'y accéder facilement (dayanta). L'entrée du temple au pied de la pagode coûte 10 CNY par personne mais ne garantit pas la montée de la pagode. Le temple est joli, il y a du monde mais pas trop. On sent la sérénité de l'endroit. Le petit jardin sur le côté permet d'admirer sous un autre angle la pagode. A l'interieur du site du temple, il y a une seconde billetterie pour pouvoir monter au sommet. Cela coûte 25 CNY par personne. L'ascension se fait par des escaliers, il n'y a pas d'ascenseur. Une fois arrivé au sommet, et, à chaque palier, vous aurez une vue dans 4 directions sur la ville de Xi'an. On peut même voir les montagnes alentour, au loin. La pagode de l'oie sauvage est un incontournable de Xi'an. Elle est le point de départ d'une très grande allée culturelle et commerciale, direction le sud de la ville.

La Gran Pagoda del Ganso Salvaje (大雁塔, Dàyàn Tǎ) es uno de los tesoros más emblemáticos de Xi’an y un símbolo vivo de la antigua Ruta de la Seda. Construida en el siglo VII durante la dinastía Tang, servía para guardar los sutras budistas que el monje Xuanzang trajo desde la India tras años de viaje. Hoy sigue siendo un lugar donde historia, espiritualidad y arquitectura se entrelazan de forma única. Pasear una mañana lluviosa por sus jardines es viajar directamente al corazón cultural de China. 🏯✨

처음 방문하는 대안탑 입장료 10 탑내부 25 다옌 탑(大雁塔)은 지금의 시안(西安) 근교인 옛 한나라의 도읍 장안(長安)에 위치한다. 서기 648년, 당나라 고종 황제 치세 때 건축을 시작하여 그로부터 4년 후에 축조한 탑은 중국 불교 탑의 전통이 어디에 뿌리를 두고 있는지를 보여주고 있다. 대부분의 당대(唐代) 건축물들은 다옌 탑처럼 단순한 디자인이었으나 그 이후 세기에 들어서면서 갈수록 정교해진다. 진흙과 벽돌로 지은 원래의 탑 구조는 모두 5층이었으나, 훗날 701 혹은 704개의 잿빛 벽돌로 재건되면서 7층 64미터의 높이로 더 높아졌다. 다옌 탑은 현장법사가 인도에서 가져온 산스크리트어 불경을 모시기 위한 용도로 지은 것이다. 오늘날에도 볼 수 있는 것으로, 다옌 탑은 각 층에서 솟아나온 작은 지붕들의 윤곽이 명확하다. 그 위로 아치형의 출입구가 벽마다 나 있다. 지상층에 나 있는 네 개의 문 위 상인방에는 부처의 형상과 그 외의 건축적 디자인을 섬세하게 새겼는데, 개중에는 당나라 명필인 저수량(596~658년)의 휘호를 음각한 석판도 보인다. 오늘날 우리가 보는 단순하면서도 엄숙한 다옌 탑은 여전히 주변 경관을 내려다보며 인도에서 중국으로 넘어온 불교의 가르침과 건축의 정신에 대해 말해 주고 있다. "이 높은 탑은 푸른 하늘을 한없이 꿰뚫고, 거센 바람은 쉼 없이 불어오네." 두보(杜甫), 시인

Wielka Pagoda Dzikich Gęsi to jedno z najbardziej charakterystycznych miejsc w Xi’an i prawdziwy symbol miasta. Jej monumentalna sylwetka wznosząca się ponad świątynne zabudowania robi ogromne wrażenie, a świadomość, że została zbudowana już w VII wieku, tylko dodaje uroku. To tutaj przechowywano cenne sutry i relikwie buddyjskie przywiezione z Indii przez słynnego mnicha, co czyni to miejsce niezwykle ważnym historycznie i duchowo. Spacer po kompleksie świątynnym pozwala poczuć spokój i wyjątkową atmosferę – piękne ogrody, pachnące kadzidła i dźwięki modlitw tworzą niepowtarzalny klimat. Sama pagoda daje też możliwość wejścia na górę, skąd rozciąga się piękny widok na Xi’an i jego okolice. To miejsce, które łączy historię, religię i architekturę w wyjątkowy sposób. Wielka Pagoda Dzikich Gęsi to obowiązkowy punkt zwiedzania dla każdego, kto chce lepiej zrozumieć kulturę i tradycję Chin.

La Grande Pagoda dell’Oca Selvatica, situata a Xi’an, è uno dei monumenti più famosi della Cina antica. Costruita nel VII secolo, serviva per conservare testi buddhisti portati dall’India. La sua struttura in mattoni, semplice ma imponente, riflette l’eleganza dell’architettura Tang. Oggi è una meta turistica e religiosa di grande importanza storica e culturale.

Great place to visit at night 大雁塔位于唐长安城（今陕西省西安市）晋昌坊的大慈恩寺内，又名“慈恩寺塔”。唐永徽三年（652年），玄奘为保存由天竺经.着七层的外观至今[17][18]。大雁塔通高64.517米，底层边长25.5米。 大雁塔作为现存最早、规模最大的唐代四方楼阁式砖塔，是佛塔这种古印度佛寺的建筑形式随佛教传入中原地区，并融入华夏文化的典型物证，是凝聚了中国古代劳动人民智慧结晶的标志性建筑，也是丝绸之路鼎盛时期东西方文化交流的重要见证。 据《大慈恩寺三藏法师传》载：古印度摩揭陀国曾有众僧掩埋坠雁并建灵塔的事，雁塔之名或即源于此。 唐永徽三年（652年），玄奘法师为供奉从天竺带回的佛像、舍利和梵文经典，在长安慈恩寺的西塔院建造了一座五层砖塔。和宝鸡的法门寺因塔建寺相反，大雁塔是因寺建塔。 除了保存从天竺取回的贝多罗树叶梵文经，大雁塔内还存有舍利子万余颗。

La Pagoda della Grande Oca Selvatica è una torre pendente e uno dei simboli della città di Xi'an. 大雁塔(大慈恩寺)，是玄奘天竺經絲綢之路後帶回長安的經卷佛像，為了妥善保存而修建了大雁塔，參考古印度佛寺的建築形式，成為唐代四方樓閣式磚塔。玄奘在此專門從事譯經和藏經之處。有亞洲最大的噴泉廣場和最大的水景廣場。保存絲路文化與大乘佛教在中國的主要意義。每小時的音樂噴泉值得一看。 開放時間：每日09:00～17:00 門票：大慈恩寺50元/人，大雁塔40元/人

西安の世界遺産。大雁塔 唐の時代の残っている建物はこの大雁塔と小雁塔のみ。 西遊記のモデルの玄奘三蔵がインドから持ち帰った経典や仏像を納める為に建てられた塔。 地震で手前に少し傾斜してるそう‥中の階段で上がる事が出来る。西安の街並みが見える。 唐の末期の戦乱で経典は今は数枚しか現存していないし仏像も無いとガイドは言っていた。 写真撮影が出来なかったが、木の薄い物にサンスクリット語でとても細かい‥丸い文字がびっしりと書かれていた。色は金色。 これを生涯かけて漢字に翻訳したそう。 ちなみに玄奘三蔵の遺骨の一部、頭蓋骨を第二次世界大戦中、日本軍が中国南京で稲荷神社を建てようとして発見。 その後さいたま市岩槻の慈恩寺へ分骨され納められた。 更に奈良の薬師寺に分骨されて、中国と日本で13ヶ所に分骨されている。

Dayan Pagoda atau Pagoda Angsa Liar Raksasa atau Pagoda Angsa Liar Besar adalah pagoda Buddha yang terletak di selatan Xi'an , Shaanxi , Cina, sekitar 4 km dari pusat kota. Dibangun pada tahun 652 pada jaman dinasti Tang dan awalnya memiliki lima lantai. Struktur ini dibangun kembali pada tahun 704 pada masa pemerintahan Permaisuri Wu Zetian dan fasad bata eksteriornya direnovasi selama Dinasti Ming . Menara ini berada di dalam kompleks Kuil Daci'en ("belas kasihan dan kebaikan"). Kuil Daci'en dibangun pada 648 untuk menghormati Permaisuri Zhangsun. Mengapa disebut Pagoda Angsa Liar Raksasa ?, berdasarkan legenda kuno umat Buddha, ada dua pemahaman, salah satunya makan daging bukanlah hal yang tabu. Suatu hari, mereka tidak dapat menemukan daging untuk dibeli. Saat melihat sekelompok angsa liar besar terbang, seorang bhikkhu berkata pada dirinya sendiri: 'Hari ini kami tidak punya daging. Saya berharap Bodhisattva yang pengasih akan memberi kita beberapa. Pada saat itu juga, angsa liar terdepan mematahkan sayapnya dan jatuh ke tanah. Semua bhikkhu terkejut dan percaya bahwa Bodhisattva menunjukkan semangatnya untuk menyuruh mereka menjadi lebih taat. Mereka mendirikan pagoda tempat angsa liar jatuh dan berhenti makan daging. Untuk mencapai Dayan Pagoga dapat menggunakan Metro sbb : Naik Metro Jalur 3 & Jalur 4 ke Stasiun Dayanta secara langsung. Ambil Metro Jalur 2 ke Stasiun Xiaozhai (Exit C) dan berjalan ke arah timur selama 10 menit.

门票40，淡季30 大雁塔位于大慈恩寺内，又名“慈恩寺塔”。唐永徽三年（652年），玄奘为保存由天竺经 丝绸之路 带回长安的经卷佛像主持修建了大雁塔，最初五层，后加盖至九层，再后层数和高度又有数次变更，最后固定为今天所看到的七层塔身。 大雁塔是砖仿木结构的四方形楼阁式塔，由塔基、塔身、塔刹三部分组成。全塔通高64.7米，塔基高4.2米，南北长约48.7米，东西长约45.7米；塔身底层边长25.5米，呈方锥形；塔刹高4.87米。1、2两层有9间，3、4两层有7间，5、6、7、8层有五间，每层四面均有劵门。

La Gran Pagoda del Ganso Salvaje se encuentra al sur de la ciudad de Xian, dentro del complejo del Templo Da Cien. Construida originalmente en el año 648 (Dinastía Tang) la pagoda que ha llegado a nuestros días data del 708 año. Con cerca de 64 m de altura y 7 pisos, la Gran Pagoda del Ganso Salvaje destaca arquitectónicamente por estar hecha de barro y refuerzos de ladrillos. Debe su fama a la importancia que tuvo durante muchos siglos dentro del budismo en China por ser el lugar donde proceden la mayoría de los antiguos textos sagrados (Sutras) traducidos al chino. Este periodo de esplendor se debe a Xuan Zang, un monje erudito que trajo los primeros Sutras o textos sagrados budistas a China desde el Tíbet para su traducción. La Gran Pagoda del Ganso Salvaje se localiza dentro del complejo del Templo Da Cien. Construido en el año 589, es también considerado uno de los templos más antiguos de todo Xian. Con cerca de 50.000 metros cuadrados, dentro del complejo también destacan el Salón Principal o Salón Mahavira, la Sala del Sermón, el Campanario, la Torre del Tambor y la zona conocida como el Bosque de la Pagodas (un rincón del complejo donde se encuentran 9 pagodas pequeñas y que guardan las reliquias de los primeros 9 abades del templo).

Elle a été reconstruite entre 701 et 704 de l'ordre de l'impératrice Wu Tian Ze.

Изначально у пагоды было 5 этажей, далее по указанию правительницы Китая были достроены ещё 2 этажа, но землятресением был разрушен один этаж, а так же пагода наклонилась. Постепенно наклон уменьшается за счёт тяжёлого сферического фундамента и пагода выравнивания. Сейчас за отдельную плату в 25 юаней (цена на 21.09.19) можно подняться на 6 этаж по узким деревянным лестницам и полюбоваться видами города. Рядом действующий будистский монастырь. 唐永徽三年（652）造，别名大慈恩寺塔。四方阁楼式砖塔，玄奘为保存经卷佛像建造，最初五层，后来曾经加至九层，现在为7层，高64.517米，底层边长25.5米。 唐永徽三年（652年），玄奘为保存由天竺经丝绸之路带回长安的经卷佛像主持修建了大雁塔，其层数经数次变更固定为现在的七层。大雁塔作为现存最早、规模最大的唐代四方楼阁式砖塔，是佛塔这种古印度佛寺的建筑形式随佛教传入中原地区，并融入华夏文化的证据。

Der Springbrunnen ist mit im Boden eingelassenen Düsen zu verschiedenen Formationen fähig und wird mit Lichteffekten sowie Musik bereichert. Vor dem Hintergrund der tausendjährigen Pagode ergibt sich ein fantastisches Bild.
